The game's first instruction, where the loader hands over. Blanks the screen, banks everything to RAM ($01 = $24), clears zero page, then lays memory out for play with copy_pages: $8000-$9FFF to $E000-$FFFF (level tables and pieces, under the KERNAL), $A000-$AFFF to $C000-$CFFF (wave and path tables), $7C00-$7DFF to $D200-$D3FF and $5C00-$67FF to $D400-$DFFF (both under the I/O), $4800-$4BFF to $A600-$A9FF and $7400-$77FF to $AA00-$ADFF, and copies the 256 bytes at $1000 to $0800 (the random byte table) with copy_bytes. Then spreads the status font (spread_font), copies the logo into it (copy_logo_glyphs), and falls into restart.

Also the RESET vector and the CBM80 entry at $8000. Banks in the I/O ($01 = $25), selects video bank 1 ($4000-$7FFF) through CIA 2, sets the music volume (init_vars), points the IRQ at title_irq ($3F93), NMI at an RTI (RESTORE does nothing), RESET and the cartridge vectors at itself, enables the raster interrupt at line $80 and switches off the CIA interrupts. Rebuilds $5C00-$67FF from $5000-$5BFF (thicken_shapes), clears the screen, prints both scores, and sets one player ($5C = 1).

The title sequence, the game's outer loop. Resets the stack, points read_stick at both ports again, colours the status lines and prints "Player1" and "Player2" over the scores game_start printed, colours the colour icon (colour_icons) and builds the giant message's map (build_message). Then loops: the title page with the music (title_page), the giant scrolling message (level 0, message_page), the hall of fame, and a demo flight (demo); the option icons are printed inside those pages, and fire on any of them starts a game at new_game.

Starts a game: copies the nine-byte player template at $3496 (score 0, wave 0, three lives, level 1) into both players' saved states ($0250, $0260) and the current state at $20-$28. Switches the sound to effects ($90 = $12), prints player 2's lives, sets the playfield character set operand of the raster interrupt ($3F4A = $2F), makes player 1 current ($5D) in game mode 2 ($5A), prints both scores and falls into next_turn.

Chooses whose turn it is and loads that player's saved state into $20-$28: player 1 from $0250 (score printed at column 1), player 2 from $0260 (column $1F). With one player ($5C = 1) it is always player 1; with two it is the player in $5D, passing over a player with no lives left ($0255, $0265). When no player has lives left it goes back to the title. In two-stick mode ($5C = 0) it rewrites read_stick's two port operands: player 1 reads $DC01 (port 1), player 2 $DC00 (port 2).

Starts a life: the title interrupt, an empty status line and the lives, the status colours of the current player (status_colours), then the launch screen: "Player 1" or "Player 2", the lives left and "Game On!", with the Manta's sprite (record $32CC). Waits for fire to be released, stirs the random table (stir_random), plays effects 3, 4 and 5, and waits for fire or about four seconds ($62 from $BF). Then builds the Dreadnought (level_setup), starts its wave list (waves_start), runs the launch out of the transporter (launch_sequence), sets the Manta's movement limits from $32ED into $35-$3C and enters the play loop.

The play loop, once a frame: waits for the frame flag $2F to clear (at line 97, irq_frame_start), then draws the shots (draw_bullets), scrolls (scroll_step), copies the map to the screen (draw_map), draws the stars (draw_stars), the generator ports (draw_ports) and the enemies (enemies_frame); counts the frame ($62), reads the stick, calls one of eight routines in turn by the frame counter (table $36CD/$36D5, through the operand at $0D25), then fire, vertical movement, speed, manoeuvres and the Manta's sprites, and the landing check. A pass sometimes takes longer than a frame: 382 passes in 400 frames from play-level1.vsf. Leaves when the Manta is lost ($32) or the Dreadnought is destroyed ($85 bit 7, end_level).
The low byte of the play loop's rotating call, written each frame from $36CD by the frame counter.

The high byte of the rotating call (from $36D5); the eight targets, one a frame in turn, are status_line, wave_control, print_score, pause_check (twice), rts_2bbe, spawn_mine and port_colour. After it: the stick-driven controls (fire_control, manta_vertical, manta_speed, manta_limits, manta_animate), landing_check, and the loop's exits.

After the play loop. If the level was finished ($27 differs from $26) moves to it; after level 15 it goes back to level 1 and adds $10 to the difficulty $28 while that stays below $40; then wave 0 and start_life. Otherwise the Manta was lost: manta_explodes, the wave index $24 goes back four (not below 0), and a life is taken from $25 (BCD). With none left, "Player N" and "Game Over!" are shown for a few seconds and the hall of fame is checked (enter_hiscore). Either way the state is saved to the player's slot and, with two players, the turn passes to the other (next_turn).
The Dreadnought has been destroyed: runs the landing, bonus and destruction sequence (dreadnought_destruct), clears $32 and goes back to life_over, which moves on to the next level.

Sound driver, called once a frame from the raster interrupt (handlers $3F00 and $3F93). $90 is the sound mode: 0 silences everything; 1 plays the music, stepping the song every fifth call ($F2) and then running the voices; 2 and 3 run the voices for sound effects only. A request of $11 or $13 starts the song from its first row at the music volume $95 (mode 1 or 3), $12 switches to effects at full volume. Each mode change goes through sound_reset.

Music sequencer, every fifth frame. $3E99 is the row of the song list $3D2C (three pattern numbers a row, one per voice, $FF ends the song and stops the music); $3E9A = $FE asks for the next row. For each voice it counts down the note length $F6,x; at zero it reads the next byte of the voice's pattern through $F3/$FC: a $00 byte is followed by a control byte whose low three bits set the octave ($F9,x) and high nibble the instrument ($A4,x); $FF ends the pattern and fetches the next song row; any other byte is a note, length in its high nibble (0 means 16) and pitch in its low nibble, looked up in $3D10/$3D00 and halved once per octave step. The pitch is written into the instrument's sound record (pointer $3D25/$3D1E) and the instrument's effect number ($27 + instrument) is requested on that voice through $91,x.

Runs the three SID voices for one frame. Writes the volume $EF to $D418, ORed with the operand at $0F5F, which is $80 (voice 3 cut off from the output) while voice 3 serves as the random-number generator and 0 while it sounds. Starts any requested effect ($91-$93): a request with bit 7 set always starts, others only when the voice's current effect ($96-$98) is not a forced one. Then for each sounding voice: adds the frequency step to the frequency and the pulse step to the pulse width (turning the pulse step round at the ends of its range), counts down the gate time ($99,x) and drops the gate when it runs out, counts down the step time ($C4) to either restart the frequency or reverse both steps, and counts down the duration ($C6); at the end it silences the voice, starts the effect chained after it ($CE) and, on voice 3, gives the voice back to the noise generator.

The operand of ORA #$00 in voices_frame: $80 mutes voice 3's output while it is the noise generator (sound_reset), 0 once an effect is started on it (start_effect). The rest of voices_frame follows: the requests, then each voice's frequency, pulse, gate, step and duration.

Starts sound effect $96,y on voice Y. Its 16-byte record is at $39AB + 16 x (number - 1): byte 0 picks the voice set-up (start_voice), bytes 1-15 are copied into the voice's state block at $C0 + 0/$0F/$1E (start frequency, frequency step, step time, duration, pulse width, pulse step, step mode, restart frequency, chained effect). Starting an effect on voice 3 takes it off the noise generator by clearing the operand at $0F5F.
Silences the SID voice whose register offset is in $A1: attack, decay, sustain and release to zero, then the test bit on and off to stop the oscillator.

Sets up a SID voice for an effect: A x 4 indexes the voice set-ups at $3947 (waveform, attack/decay, sustain/release, gate time). Silences the voice, writes $08 0 0 0 from $114A into its frequency and pulse registers, then the waveform and envelope, keeps the gate time in $99,x and the waveform in $9C,x, and writes the waveform again with the gate bit set to start the note.
$A1 = the SID register offset of voice $9F (0, 7 or 14, from $1141).

Sets the sound mode $90 to the low nibble of A and clears everything: all 25 SID registers, the current effects $96-$98 and the requests $91-$93; mutes voice 3 ($80 into the operand at $0F5F) and gives it back to the noise generator.
Voice 3 as the random-number generator: frequency $FFFF, pulse 0, noise waveform with the gate on, so that $D41B reads a fresh random byte. Its output is muted by bit 7 of $D418.

Per voice: the SID register offset (0, 7, 14), the offset of its state block from $C0 (0, $0F, $1E), and the last byte of that block ($0E, $1D, $2C, start_effect copies backwards). Then $114A: $08 0 0 0, the frequency and pulse bytes start_voice writes first, in reverse order.
Each voice's state block offset from $C0: 0, $0F, $1E (part of sid_voice_offsets).
Each voice's last state byte, $0E, $1D, $2C: start_effect copies a record backwards from there.
The four bytes start_voice writes first into a voice's frequency and pulse registers: $08, 0, 0, 0, read backwards.

The bonus game after landing. Puts up the chamber: its screen from $A6A0 (the copy of the loaded screen at $4800) and its characters from $D200 to $7C00, fading the colours in over five steps ($38DE, $38E3, $38E8). Then six steps ($A9), from the bottom row of slots up, with a countdown $A8 from 9 that steps every 256 - $AE frames ($AE from chamber_speeds by level and difficulty). At each step a value and "Quit" flash alternately in the row's two slots (which side is random, $AC); the value is the countdown plus the bonus so far $AD, which starts at the level number, in hundreds. Fire while the value is lit takes it into $AD and goes to the next step; fire on "Quit" ends with the bonus; the countdown reaching 0 ends with nothing ($A8 = 0).
Writes $AA as two decimal digits, as the chamber's digit characters ($80 + digit), into $3928/$3929.
Draws four characters at ($14) and their colour at ($1C): "Quit" from $392C when the lit side is the quit side ($AB = $AC), else the value from $3928, in the step's colour $3930.
Blanks four characters at ($14), colour black at ($1C).

The chamber's countdown: when the counter $62 wraps, one less ($A8), its digit's glyph from $3C8B into the countdown character, effect $15, the counter reloaded from $AE, and four bytes at $491C-$4963 (the screen cells of the countdown's moving marks) moved two places.

Copies the URIDIUM logo into the status font: play characters $00-$08 ($7800) become the top halves $31-$39 ($7188) and $0A-$12 ($7850) the bottom halves $B1-$B9 ($7588); characters $09 and $13 become $7D and $FD. The strings print the logo as codes $31-$39, $7D.
A frame on a still screen: reads the stick, updates the status line, waits about $18 x 1,280 cycles and counts the frame $62.

A frame of the end-of-level flight: as the play loop (bullets, scroll, map, stars, ports, pause) but the horizontal input, which sets the speed, comes from $5F instead of the stick; fire, vertical movement and speed as in play.
A frame with no input at all ($16 = $17 = 0): bullets, scroll, map, stars, ports, stick read for fire only, then vertical movement, speed and the Manta's collision test.

After a landing. The Manta drifts down onto the runway: frames run on autopilot (frame_autopilot), the height $3D lowered by one every fourth frame until it is below 5, then 160 frames more. The sprites go and the screen is wiped from both sides (shift_rows_left, shift_rows_right, 31 times) into the fuel rod chamber (fuel_rod_chamber). If the countdown ran out there ($A8 = 0) the Manta is lost (out_of_time). Otherwise "Destruct sequence primed!", then the formation annihilation bonus (one count for each formation destroyed, $87) and the ship destruct bonus (the chamber's $AD), each counted up in hundreds (count_bonus). Then the take-off: the Dreadnought's shapes and colours back, the Manta climbs out and turns, and flies the length of the Dreadnought while it vaporises behind it (vaporise_column) with random half-loops and effects, until the left end of the map; then the next level ($27) and the play loop ends ($32).
The fuel rod chamber's countdown reached zero: the play screen is put back and $32 set with the level unchanged, so life_over treats it as a Manta lost.

The chamber wipe's left half: shifts the screen and colour rows from row 2 on, columns 0-29, one character to the left, narrowing by one row each time from $1E down to 9, with a space and colour $F8 at the right end.
The wipe's right half: shifts each row's columns from $1D to $26 one character to the right, from row 2 on.

The landing, once a frame in play. Until the level's last wave has been launched ($85 = 0) it watches the wave list for its end marker, then sets $85 = 1. From then on "Land now!" flashes in the status line (on for 16 frames in 32, with effect $8F), and the Manta lands when it is over the runway's end character $6F flying level and facing right ($45 = 1): $85 = $80, which ends the play loop; any fighters still flying explode.
Never reached: an RTS ends landing_check before it and no code branches here. It would set the kill counter $88 to $FF when it is zero. The code after it is landing_check's "Land now!" flashing.
Part of landing_check, while waiting for the landing: at frame $00 of each 32 the status message is cleared (string $3150), at frame $10 "Land now!" (string $315E) is printed with effect $8F.

Destroys one column of the Dreadnought behind the departing Manta, at the map address $89/$8A (moving left by one each call, stopping at $8220): in each of the 17 rows, from the height $A4D0 for that row, three non-space characters become random wreckage ($F9-$FE) and the three above become spaces.
Sets the start of the vaporising ($89/$8A = $83E0) and a ragged edge for it: a random walk of 17 heights between 0 and 16, from 8, into $A4D1-$A4E1.

Counts a bonus up: shows "100 X n = n00" with the count $8F as two digits (the operands of the string at $3868), then for each count adds 100 to the score (add_score, entry 4), reprints the score and waits, until the count is 0.
Waits for the frame flag $2F to clear, blacks the background, and points the IRQ vector at title_irq for the screens outside play.
Waits for the frame flag to clear, sets the raster line to 252 and points the IRQ vector at irq_bottom: the three-handler chain of play.

At game over: compares the score $20-$23 with the hall of fame's eight entries (22-byte string records from $35F0 to $368A, each followed by its score as four BCD bytes) from the bottom up, moving lower entries down a place. If it made the list: "You have amassed a great score!", "Please enter your initials." and three letters (enter_letter), then the entry's initials and digits are written, and a new best score also becomes the status line's hi-score string ($352A) and the giant message's ("High - ...", $34C3).

Enter one initial: the stick up or down steps through the 27 characters at $38C3 (A-Z and a space), shown in the string at $38BA with flashing colours (cycle_colours); fire takes it, and the entry also ends after $59 x 256 frames.
Rotates five colours from the table at $37B3 by the frame counter into $37A2-$37AC and colours 17 rows from them: the flashing of the hall-of-fame entry.
Prints the lives $25 (BCD, a leading zero as a space) beside the ship icon of the current player's corner: "1up" at the left for player 1, "2up" at the right for player 2.

Adds score entry Y to the BCD score $20-$23: $38ED,y to the hundreds and thousands byte $22, $38F9,y to the tens and units byte $23, carrying up; past 99999999 the score sticks at 99999999. A carry out of $22 (another 10,000 points) gives an extra life: $25 + 1, the lives reprinted and effect $81.

Starts the current level's waves: the wave list pointer $6D/$6E from $C100/$C110 by level $26, no formations destroyed yet ($87), not landing ($85 = 0), no wave in flight ($6C = $80, $68 = $80), then copies the level's tile set into the playfield characters (copy_tile_set).

Copies four pages, the level's tile set from the page $E040 names for level $26 ($D400, $D800 or $DC00), to $7C00-$7FFF: the playfield's characters $80-$FF. Runs with every ROM and the I/O banked out, since the sets lie under the I/O.

Every 64 frames (at phase $21 of the frame counter $62): when the last wave has gone ($6C = $80) counts it as destroyed ($87) if every fighter was shot ($88 = 0) and it was not a filler wave ($68 = 0), then marks no wave; when there is none ($6C = 0) starts the next one at new_wave.

Launches a formation. Reads the next wave number from the level's list ($6D),$24 (and advances $24); $FF, the end of the list, gives one of the filler waves $12-$15 at random, marked in $68 so that it scores no formation bonus. The 16-byte record at $C200 + 16 x number holds six path numbers (0 for no fighter), the spacing in frames between fighters (byte 12), the entry side (byte 13: 0 the side the Manta faces, $FF behind it, anything else at random), the type (byte 14) and six start heights (bytes 6-11, 0 for the Manta's height). The type picks, from the tables at $36F3 on, the horizontal speed ($66, and $63 its negative), the vertical speed ($82, $80 its negative), the firing chance ($69, plus half the lives, the level and the difficulty), the bullet shape ($6A), the score ($7F) and the bullet's speed ($65). Each fighter gets its path pointer from $C120/$C190, state 2, a start delay and its sprite; requests effect $AE.

Runs the six enemy sprites (0-5), once a frame: for each one in use ($A490,y non-zero) reads its sprite (sprite_get) and calls the handler for its state through the table at $36E5, written into the JSR at $1C2B: 2 a fighter following its path (fighter_move), 4 an enemy bullet (bullet_move), 6 an explosion (explosion_move), 8 a mine materialising (mine_appear), 10 a homing mine (mine_move).
Low byte of enemies_frame's handler call, written from enemy_state_handlers by the sprite's state.
High byte of the handler call; after the call, the loop moves on to the next of the six sprites.
State 6, an explosion: moves with the Dreadnought, and every other frame steps the shape $0E on; at shape $1E the sprite is switched off and its slot freed ($6C counted down).
Adds the scroll speed $2E (signed) to the sprite's 9-bit X in $05/$06, so that it keeps its place over the Dreadnought.

State 2, a fighter. Moves it with the scroll and by its velocity (move_by_velocity), then follows its path: when its step timer $A4B0 runs out it reads the next path byte through ($70,x): $FF holds the last step; otherwise bits 0-6 are the step's flags ($A4B8) and with bit 7 set the next byte is the step's length (else 1 frame). Flags: 1 accelerate along $63/$64, 2 along $66/$67 (one way or the other), 4 down by $82, 8 up by $80, $10 fire once, $20 stop dead, $40 steer towards the Manta's height. Every eighth frame (on its own phase) it may fire, when a random byte is below the chance $69. Then finds the character under the sprite: one of the Manta's bullets ($10-$1F) means it is shot: the bullet is put out, the type's score added (none in a filler wave), effect $26, state 6 explosion and one fewer fighter left ($88). Off the visible screen it is either turned to face back (first time) or removed.
Shared end of the enemy handlers: a sprite whose X has passed $19C-$1C3 (off the right edge, in the border) is switched off and its slot freed. Writes the sprite back (sprite_put).

State 4, an enemy bullet: moves with the scroll and by its velocity for its lifetime $A4B0; if it touches the Manta (hits_manta) while the Manta is low (height $3D below $14) the Manta is lost ($32). At the end of its time it turns into an explosion (state 6) with effect $0A.
Adds sprite Y's velocity to its position: X ($05/$06) by the 16-bit $A498/$A4A8, Y ($07) by $A4A0 (with the carry of the fraction $A4C8).

A fighter fires: takes a free sprite slot (0-5) if there is one, places a bullet there with the wave's bullet shape $6A at the fighter's position, moving at the fighter's speed plus the bullet speed $65, state 4 with a lifetime of $A0 frames, and requests effect $0B.
State 8, a mine materialising over its generator port: moves with the scroll and every fourth frame steps its shape down from $1D; at $13 it becomes a homing mine (state 10, shape $11).

Called in turn from the play loop every eighth frame: while no formation is flying ($6C bit 7) and with a chance of a quarter of $69, takes a generator port that is on screen ($0240,x positive, from the last of the $54 found) and starts a mine materialising over it in a free sprite slot (state 8, shape $1D, effect $0D), with a lifetime from the level and difficulty.

Carry set when the sprite touches the Manta: its X must be between $A2 and $B1 on the left of the screen (where the Manta always is) and its Y within the box the tables $374F and $3747 give for its shape around the Manta's Y $33.

State 10, a homing mine: moves with the scroll and by its velocity, steers towards the Manta (home_in), counts down its lifetime (with effect $0E at intervals), and like a bullet destroys a low Manta it touches. At the end it explodes.

Every fourth frame turns the mine's velocity towards the Manta: vertical by one towards $33, horizontal by one towards the Manta's screen column ($A0-$AA), the horizontal kept within -6..6 and the vertical within -4..4.

Builds the Dreadnought for level $26 and resets the Manta: indexes the map pieces (index_pieces), map position $0040 (the left edge of the map), background $4A = $F1, builds the map (build_map), clears the piece index (clear_piece_index), sets the level's colours (level_colours), scatters the stars (make_stars), draws the first screen (draw_map, draw_stars), the star rows above and below the playfield (star_rows). Then the Manta at rest: speed 0, no manoeuvre, level and facing left ($45 = 5), as it reverses out of the transporter, height $3D = $10, Y $98, frame $59, and switches to the play interrupt.

Holds a still page for up to two times 256 frames, or until fire: each frame reads the stick and the keys, the volume keys, the status line, the player keys (option_keys) and the colour keys (colour_keys), with a delay for pacing.

Runs the giant scrolling message: level 0's map, built from letter pieces, scrolls past at the speed set by the caller ($2E = -4) with the stars and the status line, the option, volume and colour keys working, until fire or the end of the map.

The demo flight. Game mode 1 ($5A), score and wave 0, a level from 1 to 8 picked by the random byte at $0800, built as for play; the Manta and its shadow placed from records, then up to eight times 256 frames of play driven by demo_stick instead of the joystick, the real stick still read for fire, which ends the demo (and starts a game). A Manta lost also ends it with the explosion.
Low byte of the demo's rotating call, from $36DD by the frame counter (four targets: status_line, spawn_mine, colour_keys, option_keys).

High byte of the demo's rotating call (from $36E1); then the demo's pilot (demo_stick), fire, vertical, speed, limits and animation of the Manta, and the demo's exits: the Manta lost, or the time used up.

The demo's pilot: fire toggled at random about one frame in four ($8E), and each of the vertical and horizontal directions kept from the last frame ($5E, $5F) except when a random byte of $B4 or more picks a new one (-1, 0 or +1).

Every 128 frames steps the message in the middle of the second status line on ($5B, 0-3): the URIDIUM logo; "Hi-score"; the best score and its initials; then in play (mode 2) the level's name, otherwise the joystick icons of the player option ($5C, strings $353A, $354B, $355E) with the colour or black-and-white icon. In game mode 3 (paused) it shows the logo. "Demo" in the top line is printed by the title loop.

The player options on the title screens. F1 alone: one player ($5C = 1); SHIFT and F1 (F2): two players sharing one joystick ($5C = 2); F3: two players with a joystick each ($5C = 0). F1 and F2 also point read_stick at both ports. Each prints its icon in the status line.
Fills 21 rows of the screen from $48A0 (below the top status line) with A.
Colours Y + 1 screen rows, from the colour RAM address in $1C/$1D, each with the colour the table at ($1A) gives for it, last row first.
F7 sets colour ($61 = 0, "Colour"), SHIFT and F7 (F8) black and white ($61 = $FF, "Blck-Whte"), and updates the icons (colour_icons). Black and white makes level_colours use scheme 0 for every level.
An RTS nothing reaches: the routine before it ends with a JMP.
Colours the two icon cells of the top status line ($D85A, $D85B, $D882, $D883) grey for black and white, or in colours.

Builds the giant message's map list at $8010 from the text at $349F ("Uridium by Andrew Braybrook. High - 12000 AEB" in the game's alphabet, ending with a negative byte): for each character, the table at $C000 gives an offset into the letter pieces at $C060, four piece numbers per letter, of which the non-zero ones are written, then piece 1 (a gap). Four zeros end it. Level 0's piece list ($E010) points here.

The Manta is lost: its sprites become an explosion of eight sprites thrown out at random around it, with effect $0C on two voices, while the Dreadnought coasts to a stop (frame_coast), for six frames plus 16 more; in two-player games the score is reprinted. Fire can cut it short except in play.
Steps the generator ports' flashing colour $55 through the eight colours at $36C5, one step every eight frames.
Fills the two rows above the playfield ($48A0) and the two below ($4B98) with random stars (star_row), and clears the six cells of $4BAC and $4BD4 (under the bottom status).

Up and down. Normally the stick ($16) changes the vertical velocity $34 by one a frame, up to the limits $35 (up) and $36 (down) from the level's movement table; with the stick centred the velocity is halved towards zero each frame. When fire has been held for seven frames ($49 reaches 0, fire_control) up or down instead asks for a roll: from level flight to edge-on in the direction pushed, or back to level, as long as the speed $3E is at least 3 and no manoeuvre is running ($3F, $45 bit 7).
Rebuilds $5C00-$67FF from $5000-$5BFF: every byte ORed with itself with each pair of bits swapped, so that any pixel set in a pair sets both. Run at every restart.

Left and right change the speed $2D/$2E (signed, pixels a frame and a fraction): with the Manta facing one way ($45 bit 2 clear) by $39 or $3A, facing the other by $3B or $3C. During a half-loop the manoeuvre's own acceleration $3F is added instead, which carries the Manta through the turn. Keeps the size of the speed in $3E.

Moves the Manta vertically by $34 and keeps its Y between $62 and $D7; keeps the speed within the limits $37 and $38. Near the ends of the map, unless a manoeuvre is running: with the speed positive (the map position $29/$2A falling), a position below $0100 sets the push $3F = $C8 and one from $0E80 up asks for a half-loop; with it negative, below $0080 asks for a half-loop and from $0E00 up sets $3F = $38. Below speed 2 ($3E) it asks for a half-loop that reverses the direction (bit 2 of $45), and at speed 2 brings an edge-on Manta back level.

Starts and steps the Manta's manoeuvres. A request ($46 bit 7) picks the animation from the tables $3292/$32A4 (facing right, $45 bit 2 clear) or $3266/$327C (facing left), by the current roll position (bits 0-1 of $45) and the requested one: each sequence is a length, the frames, whether the height changes and the push $3F. While one runs (bit 7 of $45) it steps every other frame: the frame into $40 and, for a half-loop, the height $3D changed by $32F5. At the end the manoeuvre bit is cleared. Then places the Manta (sprite 6, shape $40, Y $33) and its shadow (sprite 7, shape $40 + $30, lower and further right by the height $3D) and falls into manta_collide.

The Manta against the Dreadnought: $33E8 + frame gives the collision flags (collide_shapes). Looks at the map characters under the Manta through $52/$53: the middle one always (kept in $86), the left and right ones unless bit 0 is set (an end-on frame), and the cells above and below the middle when bit 7 is set (every frame but an edge-on one). Any of the solid characters $80-$8F there destroys the Manta ($32 = $80).

The launch from the transporter: places the transporter and Manta sprites from the eight records at $3306/$3310, waits 16 frames, opens the transporter's door (sprite 6's shape stepped to $0B with effect 6), moves the Manta out to the right with effect 7, then the transporter and its parts slide away left, accelerating, with effect 8 on all voices, until off screen. Leaves sprite 6 on as the Manta with its multicolour.

One frame of a screen outside play: waits for the frame flag $2F to clear, reads the stick, checks for pause (pause_check), reads the keys, updates the status line and counts the frame, then waits for the flag to be set again.

The fire button. A press fires a pair of shots at once (manta_fire). While fire stays held $49 counts down from 7; at 0 the next up or down rolls the Manta (manta_vertical). Releasing fire re-arms it.

The operand of LDA #$07 in fire_control, the frames fire must be held before up or down rolls the Manta; other routines read it to reset $49. The rest of fire_control handles a press and a held button.

Fires up to two shots from the Manta's guns: the tables $3373 and $33A1 give, for the current frame $40, the height of each gun relative to the Manta (0 for none). Each shot takes a free bullet slot (free_bullet) and is launched (launch_bullet).
Carry clear and X = the first free bullet slot of six ($A460,x = 0), searching up from X; carry set if all are in flight.

Puts a shot into bullet slot X at the Manta's nose: its step $A460 is 2 or -2 columns a frame in the direction of flight ($2E), its map address $A430/$A440 from the Manta's map position $52/$53 and the gun's height, its pixel row in the character $A470, and the character it covers in $A450. Requests effect 9.

The Manta's shots are software sprites drawn into the map. First puts back the character each shot covers. Then moves each one by its step: outside the visible columns ($50-$51) it ends; on a wall character ($80-$8F) it ends with effect $21; on a target ($90-$9F) it destroys it (hit_feature). Otherwise it copies the character under it into its own character ($10 + slot, or $00 + slot on alternate frames) at $7800, draws the shot as two pixel rows ($00, $AA) at its row, and puts that character in the map. Alternating the two character sets of codes stops a shot flickering while the screen is copied.
The operand of ORA #$80 in draw_bullets, flipped between $80 and 0 every frame: which of the two character banks a shot's glyph is built in ($7880 + 8 x slot or $7800 + 8 x slot).
The low byte of the LDA $7800,Y in draw_bullets: the character under the shot x 8, written before the copy.
The high byte of that LDA ($78 plus the top bits of character x 8): the copy of the covered character into the shot's own character, then the two pixel rows of the shot.

The operand of ORA #$10, flipped between $10 and 0 every frame with $2A7F: the shot's character code is $10 + slot or slot. Then the loop over the six shots ends and the flips are made; the routine's last part ends a shot that hit a wall (effect $21) or left the screen.
Adds the step A (signed) to bullet X's map address $A430/$A440 and returns the new high byte, the low byte in $1C.

A shot hit target character A ($90-$9F). The tables at $33C6 on give for each the offset back to the feature's top-left corner, its width, height and score: the score is added (add_score), effect $1B played, and every character of the feature turned into its wreck (code - $20), ending any other shot found there.
Moves the map position $29/$2A by the speed $2E and sets the fine scroll $2C for $D016 from its low three bits.

RUN/STOP pauses the game: "Pause" in the status line, the sound off, mode 3. Waits for the key to be released, then until fire or RUN/STOP resumes (sound back to effects, mode 2), keeping the frame counter. CLR/HOME while paused abandons the game and goes back to the title.

An RTS: pause_check's way out when RUN/STOP is not down, and the handler of the empty enemy states 0 and 12 (enemy_state_handlers). After it, the rest of pause_check: CLR/HOME back to the title; fire or RUN/STOP to resume, the frame counter restored, sound back to effects and mode 2.

Copies the visible part of the map to the screen: from the column $29/$2A divided by 8, 17 rows of 39 characters, each row a page pair apart in the map ($8200 + $200 x row), to screen $48F0 on. The copy loop's operands are rewritten as it goes. Leaves the map address under the Manta in $52/$53 (fixed screen column $12, its row from Y $33) and the visible columns in $50/$51.
Low byte of draw_map's row source, the map column ($31).
High byte of the row source: the map row's page ($30), moved on two pages for each row.
Low byte of draw_map's screen destination, from $48F0, 40 on for each row.
High byte of the screen destination. After the 17 rows: the map address under the Manta ($52/$53) and the visible columns ($50/$51).

Makes the table of map pieces: walks the piece store at $E100 and puts each piece's address into $A400/$A500 by piece number, from 1. A piece is a count of columns, then for each column a count of characters (low five bits) and the characters, bottom up. A count of 0 ends the store.
Zeroes $A400-$A5FF, the piece index, once the map is built; the space is reused for the stars and the bullets.

Builds level $26's map at $8200-$A3FF: 17 rows of 512 columns, row r at $8200 + $200 x r. Fills columns 0-63 with spaces, then lays pieces side by side from column 64 to 511 in the order the level's list gives ($E010/$E020; a 0 repeats piece 1, empty space), each column drawn upwards from the bottom row and topped up with spaces. Then a second list places pieces at a given row and column (a byte with the row's page, a column, a piece number; spaces in the piece leave the map as it is), noting every generator port it lays (note_port).

While a piece is laid: a character $59-$5B is a generator port. Up to sixteen are recorded ($54 counts them): map column high bit $0230, screen row $0220, column $0210 and column / 2 $0200, and $0240 = $FF, not on screen.

Scatters sixteen stars for the space around the Dreadnought from the random table at $0800: for each a row 7-22 (no two in a row while it can help it, over $8D tries, pick_star_row) and a column (pick_star_column), its address in $A400/$A410/$A480 and its character, $42 or $43, in $A420.
Moves the star's row X on by 7 (wrapping within 7-22) until it finds a row with no star yet or has tried $8D times.
Moves the star's column X on by 7 (wrapping at 39) until it finds a column with no star yet or has tried $8D times.

Draws the stars over the map copy on the screen: a star goes only where the screen holds a space, in the star colour $58, and where it is covered its colour cell takes the map colour $4D. Then the fine scroll $2C picks one of the star characters' patterns from $311E, written into the three star rows of characters $42/$43 at $7A15-$7A1B, so the stars stay still while the screen scrolls by whole characters.
Fills a 39-character screen row at ($1C) with random stars from the table at $0800 (indexed by $10): mostly spaces, a star character $42 or $43 for one byte in sixteen.

Sets the Dreadnought's colours: five bytes from $3372 + 5 x the level's scheme ($E030; scheme 0 in black and white, $61) into $4B-$4F: the two multicolours ($D023, $D022), the map colour $4D (colour RAM of the 17 playfield rows), the Manta's multicolour $D025, and the enemies' colour $4F. The star colour $58 is the map colour without bit 3.

Reads RUN/STOP and CLR/HOME into $60: bit 7 clear while RUN/STOP is down (row 7), bit 3 clear while CLR/HOME is (row 6). Leaves $60 = $FF, nothing pressed, if the joystick in port 1 is pushing right, which would look like a key on these rows.

Flashes the generator ports: for each recorded port ($54 of them) puts the map colour back where it was last drawn, then, if its column is on screen, writes the flashing colour $55 into its colour cell and keeps the screen column in $0240 ($FF when off screen, which spawn_mine reads).
Colours the two status lines for the turn: the current player's corner bright and the other's dim, or with one player the player 2 corner black.
XORs every byte of the random table at $0800 with a fresh random byte from the noise voice ($D41B). The ROL/ROR pair of $800F in the loop leaves it unchanged and only spends time.

Makes the status lines' double-height font from the 8-row font at $7000: each of 128 characters becomes a top half at $7000 (its rows 0-3) and a bottom half at $7400 (rows 4-7, the code + $80), each glyph row followed by a blank row, which gives the status text its scan-line look. Run once at start-up; it overwrites the source as it goes, top half last.

The fuel rod chamber's countdown speeds, indexed by the level plus the difficulty / 16: the counter starts at the value and counts up to 256, so a digit lasts 256 minus it frames ($90 at level 1, 112 frames), down to 16 frames at $F0. The byte at $310A, index 0, is never used.

Eight single-pixel-hole bytes ($FE, $FD .. $7F), one per fine-scroll position: draw_stars writes the one for $2C into the star characters' rows, so a star seems to stay in place while the screen scrolls a whole character at a time.
String record: "Player1", row 0, column 1, the first status line's left label.
String record: "Player2", row 0, column 31.
String record: "1up", the ship icon ($7A, $7B) and the lives, row 0, column 1; print_lives writes the digits into it at $3142/$3143.
Player 1's lives, tens digit (a space for none), written by print_lives.
Player 1's lives, units digit, then the rest of the 1up string.
String record: the ship icon, the lives and "2up", row 0, column 31; print_lives writes the digits at $3149/$314A.
Player 2's lives, tens digit.
Player 2's lives, units digit, then " 2up".
String record: eleven spaces at row 0, column 15, which clears the middle of the top status line.
String record: "Land now!", row 0, column 15, flashed by land_now_flash.
Colour RAM of the top status line's first row, 40 bytes (title copies it to $D800, and without bit 3 to $D828): cyan at the corners, light red in the middle.
Colour RAM of the second status line's first row ($D850): light green corners, white middle.
Colour RAM of the second status line's second row ($D878): green corners, yellow middle.

The Manta's twelve manoeuvre animations, each a length, that many sprite frames (played last first), a byte that says whether the height changes, and the speed push $3F. Eight four-frame rolls between level and edge-on; two sixteen-frame turns through the whole roll cycle ($3211 facing right, $3253 facing left); and the two half-loops, which climb and push the speed and end facing the other way: $31FE through the end-on frames $60-$66 to the left-facing level frame $59, $3240 through $67-$6D to the right-facing $41.
Low bytes of the animation for each change of attitude while facing left ($45 bit 2 set): index = current roll (bits 0-1 of $45) x 8 + requested attitude's low three bits; 0 for none (manta_animate).
High bytes of the animations facing left.
Low bytes of the animations while facing right ($45 bit 2 clear).
High bytes of the animations facing right.
Two 11-byte sprite records (sprite, X, X high, Y, enable, expand Y, priority, multicolour, expand X, colour, shape) for sprite 6: the Manta at $70 and at $AA, shape $59.
Sprite record: sprite 6 at X $A0, Y $AE, shape $41, on the launch screen (start_life).
Sprite record: sprite 7, the Manta's shadow, X $BA, Y $A8 (the Manta's $AA, $98 moved by the height $10 and half of it), hires behind the background, colour $FB, shape $89 (demo, launch_sequence).
Sprite record: sprite 7 at X $AA for the Manta's explosion, shape $30 (manta_explodes).
The Manta's movement limits, copied to $35-$3C at each life: vertical speed -3 to +3, speed -8 to +8, and the four accelerations $B0, $40, $50, $C0.
The height change for each frame of a half-loop (manta_animate, indexed by the frames left): down to -3 and back, then up to +3 and back, so the Manta rises over the Dreadnought and comes down again.
Low bytes of the sprite records launch_sequence places: eight transporter pieces ($331A on) and, at index 8 and 9, the demo Manta ($32B6) and the shadow ($32D7).
launch_rec_lo's entry 8: the Manta's record ($32B6, facing left, shape $59), which launch_sequence places when the door has opened.
launch_rec_lo's entry 9: the shadow's record ($32D7), placed by launch_sequence and demo.
High bytes of launch_sequence's records.
launch_rec_hi's entry 8.
launch_rec_hi's entry 9.
Eight 11-byte sprite records: the transporter (sprites 0-5 at X $52-$82, Y $8D and $A2, shapes $00-$05) and the Manta inside it (sprites 6 and 7, shapes $07 and $06).

The raster interrupt for every screen that is not play (title, launch, hall of fame, chamber, bonus): $D018 = $2D, black background, $D011 = $1B, $D016 = $C8 (hires, 40 columns). It fires twice a frame, at lines 128 and 0: the operand of LDA #$80 at $3FAF is both the value put in the frame flag $2F and the next raster line, and is flipped between $80 and 0 each time. So $2F is $80 from line 128 and 0 from line 0, and the sound driver runs once a frame, at line 128; cassette_motor runs at both.
